topic: Command surfacing review pass six - scorer lineage (heredoc redirect fix, start shape split, read-alone lookup rule)

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A shell that lists two heredocs on one line is uncommon and the pre-fix pattern behaved the same way, so the gap may be accepted as out of reach; that reading leaves the fix comment (a heredoc body is data) untrue for an input the pattern claims to strip, and the false write moves the first-write boundary.
findingDetails.claim: HEREDOC_BODY keeps the rest of the opening line after the first delimiter in group 1, so a line that lists two heredocs consumes only the first body and leaves the second body in the scanned text, where a comparison reads as a redirect.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Ran the two-delimiter command through normalize, then re-read the pattern to confirm the second delimiter lands in group 1 rather than in a body. Checked the packet registry for an existing finding with this input; the recorded heredoc finding names a delimiter that is not a bare identifier, a different input.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if the corpus and runner never emit a shell command with more than one heredoc delimiter on one line.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The pattern, its redirect consumer and the shell write scanner are all inside the pass-six scoped scorer file.
findingDetails.title: A second heredoc on one opening line is not stripped, so its body comparison becomes a write

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A write with no named target is still a write, so counting it may be the conservative choice; that choice is conservative for unsafe but not for the start rule, where phase 036 defines the start as a write inside the checkout and an unknown folder is not evidence of one.
findingDetails.claim: writePaths keeps a write with no target as [null], and firstWritePosition skips a write only when its path is a string outside the checkout, so an unnamed write satisfies the inside-checkout test that startShape uses for readWrite.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Probed a Read of the command document plus a Write tool call with no path key, and a Read plus a Bash apply_patch whose body used ---/+++ headers; both produced one unnamed write and startState returned readWrite with started true. Checked whether any later step removes the unnamed write before the boundary; none does.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if every scoped runtime always records a target for a write tool call and for apply_patch.
findingDetails.scopeProof: writePaths, firstWritePosition and startShape are the scoped scorer own boundary path, and the phase 036 edge-case row names the outside-checkout write as a lookup.
findingDetails.title: A write whose target is never named counts as inside the checkout, so a lookup plus an unnamed write scores as a readWrite start

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The sentence can be read as naming the read events the start rule examines rather than claiming a bare read starts; that reading still misleads, because the same row later says a read with no write is a lookup and the test comment says a reader that opens the document is the same start a read tool records.
findingDetails.claim: The README row keeps the sentence that a cat of the command document counts as a start while the same row later states the new lookup rule, and the vitest comment above the shell-step table states the same old rule even though every case there also writes a file.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Ran the read-alone input through startState (started false, shape readOnly) and re-read the README row to confirm both sentences live in the same cell. Checked the shell-step table body to see whether the cat case writes; it does.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if the README sentence is read as a statement about which events the rule inspects rather than about sufficiency.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The README and the vitest file are both pass-six scoped scorer files, and the contradiction is inside the single README row.
findingDetails.title: The README and the shell-step test still say a bare document read is a start

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The declaration is already partial (it omits rowId, rowType and commandStarted), so one more omission may be treated as existing debt; that reading still leaves the field this branch added outside the only contract its consumer reads.
findingDetails.claim: The @returns union for scoreRun lists startRow and started but not startShape, which this branch added at line 2104 and addScored reads at line 2412 behind a !== null guard.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the whole @returns block to check whether the field is named under another word; it is not. Checked whether a missing field would throw in addScored; the !== null guard lets undefined through and the increment creates an undefined key holding NaN.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if scoreRun returns a typed object rather than the documented union.
